outcome: Experiment Authoring now has compiler-derived navigation, folding and in-artifact search
owner_impact: Configuration, Initialization, Controller and Metrics now expose a compact Outline built from the same parsers/compilers that define each artifact language. Selecting a symbol jumps to its real definition line, Find opens Ace's in-artifact search, and Python-like blocks expose fold widgets. The navigation stays secondary to the active editor and remains compact on narrow screens; source, dirty-state, autosave, revision and runtime semantics are unchanged.

next.text: #205 is the next and final currently approved code-authoring ergonomics ticket. It will connect compiler diagnostics to source locations and add constrained-language completion. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Configuration parameters, Initializer functions, Controller class/state/step symbols and Metrics declarations are exposed by their existing compiler/parser modules rather than inferred from comments or decorative headings.
React consumes one artifactStructureSafe model and renders a compact Outline selector; symbol selection calls the Ace editor's gotoLine command.
Find uses Ace's native search command rather than a second search implementation.
Ace Python mode fold widgets remain enabled and are production-smoked on the Initializer artifact.
Outline recomputation is debounced while editing and becomes unavailable rather than inventing structure when the current source no longer parses.

Production browser smoke requires a populated Configuration outline, opens the real Ace search UI, switches to Initialization and verifies exactly three compiler-derived functions plus visible fold widgets.
